markdown_content: ## Overview of Grading Display in Clo 2025.1 This section explains how to visualize grading in Clo 2025.1, including toggling grading visibility alongside graphics in the 2D window. It covers the use of the garment display toggle and how to enable grading display even without selecting grading tools. To view grading in Clo 2025.1, switch from "Monochrome" to "Front Texture Surface" in the 2D window. Then, open the garment display toggle menu (represented by a T-shirt icon) and select "Show Grading." This displays all grading information simultaneously with the garment's graphics, providing a clear overview of graded points and segments without needing to select grading tools. --- ## Introduction to the Defined Grading Tool and Graded Points This section introduces the Defined Grading Tool in Clo 2025.1, highlighting the visual cues for graded points and explaining the initial challenges users might face when adjusting grading on individual points. Upon selecting the Edit Grading Tool, all graded points are immediately visible, indicated by a green halo around each point. This signals points included in grading calculations. Adjusting a single graded point may initially appear problematic, as changes affect only that point, leading to disproportionate grading results. This behavior is due to some points being internal curve points that require specific grading settings to behave correctly. --- ## Managing Curve Points and Improving Grading Proportionality This section details how to identify and manage curve points within grading. It covers selecting multiple curve points, converting them to non-graded points, and explains how this improves proportional grading behavior. Curve points, often numerous on curved lines, can disrupt proportional grading when individually adjusted. To identify these, use the Edit Curve Grading tool, which marks curve points with red dots and green halos. Instead of adjusting points one-by-one, hold Shift and left-click each red-dot curve point to select multiple points simultaneously. Then right-click and choose "Convert to Non-Graded Point" to exclude them from grading. Converting curve points to non-graded points allows proportional grading to function correctly. When increasing or decreasing grading at a point, the adjustments now affect the surrounding graded points proportionally, eliminating erratic or localized grading changes. --- ## Best Practices for Curve Point Optimization This section explains best practices for managing curve points via the Optimize Curve Points feature to reduce excessive curve points and automate non-graded point assignment. Excessive curve points can complicate grading. Using the Edit Pattern Tool, select a curved segment (e.g., neck opening), right-click, and choose "Optimize Curve Points." This reduces the number of curve points while maintaining the curve shape. After optimization, curve points automatically convert to non-graded points, streamlining grading adjustments. This workflow allows quick proportional grading on fewer points, enhancing efficiency. For example, after optimization, you can select multiple graded points and adjust them together using keyboard arrow keys with precise increments (e.g., 0.025) to control grading changes accurately. --- ## Handling Segment Points in Grading This section describes how segment points, like curve points, can be toggled between graded and non-graded states to control grading behavior. Segment points, such as those found along necklines or armholes, also affect grading proportionality. You can right-click on any segment point and select "Convert to Non-Graded Point" to exclude it from grading, causing it to proportionally follow adjacent graded points. Reversely, you can convert non-graded segment points back to graded points via right-click. This flexibility allows fine-tuning of grading behavior for both curve and segment points, ensuring smooth proportional scaling across the garment's pattern. --- ## Manual Editing and Smoothing of Grading Points This section covers how to manually edit grading points for detailed control, including smoothing techniques and individual point adjustments. Using the Edit Grading and Edit Curve Point tools, you can manually adjust grading values for individual points. This includes smoothing transitions by lowering or raising adjacent points, enabling custom grading shapes beyond automatic proportional scaling. Zooming in during editing helps refine these adjustments precisely. This granular control provides designers with the ability to fine-tune grading to fit specific design needs while preserving overall proportionality. --- ## Workflow for Importing DXF Patterns and Preparing for Grading This section outlines a recommended workflow for importing DXF patterns into Clo and preparing them for grading using curve point optimization. When importing a DXF pattern, curve points often appear in excess and as graded points by default. After import, use the Edit Curve Point tool to assess the number of curve points, then apply the Edit Pattern Tool’s "Optimize Curve Points" function on relevant segments (e.g., back, front, sleeves). Confirm the optimization slider to preserve curve shapes. Optimized curve points automatically convert to non-graded points, simplifying grading setup. This allows you to quickly use the Edit Grading tool to add grading with proportional behavior, increasing efficiency when working with imported patterns. --- ## Efficient Grading Adjustments and Mirroring Techniques This section highlights efficient grading editing techniques such as selective point conversion, incremental keyboard input, and mirroring grading across symmetrical pattern sections. You can selectively convert points between graded and non-graded states as needed during grading adjustments. Using keyboard arrow keys with defined increments (e.g., 0.025) enables precise grading control. For symmetrical garments, copy grading values, then use right-click menus to mirror and paste grading adjustments along X and Y axes. This ensures consistent grading across pattern halves and speeds up the grading process. --- ## Summary of Key Grading Features in Clo 2025.1 - **Show Grading Toggle**: Visualize grading with garment graphics. - **Defined Grading Tool**: Edit graded points with green halo indicators. - **Curve Point Management**: Identify via Edit Curve Grading; convert to non-graded for proportional scaling. - **Optimize Curve Points**: Reduce curve points automatically, converting them to non-graded. - **Segment Point Control**: Convert between graded and non-graded to refine grading behavior. - **Manual Editing**: Smooth and adjust grading points individually. - **DXF Import Workflow**: Optimize curve points after import for clean grading setup. - **Precise Grading Input**: Use arrow keys with decimal increments. - **Mirroring Grading**: Copy and mirror grading values for symmetrical patterns. These features collectively enhance grading control, making proportional adjustments easier and more precise in Clo 2025.1.
